etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English onyoun, oynoun, from Old French oignon, from Latin ūniōnem, accusative of ūniō (“onion, large pearl”), which had also been borrowed into Old English as yne, ynnelēac (“onion”) (> Middle English hynne-leac, henne-leac). Also displaced Middle English knelek (literally “knee-leek”) and the inherited term ramsons.

definitions.definition: A monocotyledonous plant (Allium cepa), allied to garlic, used as vegetable and spice.

quote.citation: 1944, Oregon. Agricultural experiment station, Circular of Information - Issues 323-395, page 3:
quote.text: Some of the weeds that cause an undesirable flavor in milk are: onion, tarweed, scaleweed, garlic, mustard, pepper grass.

quote.citation: 2021, Rose Ray, Caro Langton, Into Green: Everyday Ways to Find and Lose Yourself in Nature, page 62:
quote.text: To get started, how about creating an edible window box? Sowed in the spring, salad seeds like radish, lettuce and spring onion will germinate so quickly that you'll be harvesting a crop in a month or two.

definitions.definition: The bulb of such a plant.

quote.citation: 1962 (quoting 1381 text), Hans Kurath & Sherman M. Kuhn, eds., Middle English Dictionary, Ann Arbor, Mich.: University of Michigan Press, ISBN 978-0-472-01044-8, page 1242:
quote.text: dorrẹ̅, dōrī adj. & n.  […]  cook. glazed with a yellow substance; pome(s ~, sopes ~.  […]  1381 Pegge Cook. Recipes p. 114: For to make Soupys dorry. Nym onyons  […]  Nym wyn  […]  toste wyte bred and do yt in dischis, and god Almande mylk.

quote.citation: 2015 September 4, “In Minnesota’s Iron Range, Midwestern With a Modern Twist”, in The New York Times‎[2]:
quote.text: Goulash, a local favorite, was brought up-to-date with seared grass-fed rib-eye, stewed cippolini onions and roasted cherry tomatoes.

definitions.definition: A plant of the genus Allium as a whole. (Can we add an example for this sense?)

quote.citation: 1846, George William MacArthur Reynolds, The Mysteries of London, page 60:
quote.text: […]  M was a Magsman, frequenting Pall-Mall; / N was a Nose that turned chirp on his pal; / O was an Onion, possessed by a swell; / P was a Pannie, done niblike and well.  […]

definitions.definition: Alternative letter-case form of Onion (“an inhabitant of Bermuda; a Bermudian”)
(4chan, slang) Soy, particularly when used in compound words related to the soy boy stereotype.
